The DNA combining mechanic is super unique and makes this game really interesting and replayable. If your a fan of tactics based games or turn based roguelites then you should definitely check this one out! https://youtu.be/5mT9ROBTbnI

TL;DR I enjoyed the game. Would even recommend it outside of one thing that ruined it for me. don't play the joker commander. Review: Gameplay is fun, music is full of bangers. lots of unlocks and powers that upgrade all the time. constantly seeing 'new' next to powers I'd never seen as I played more and more was awesome. The visuals are even clear and concise and everything is explained well. I was having a lot of fun. dear god don't play joker. it's visuals is nauseating. Yeah, its my fault for pushing through it and trying to beat the game, but not being able to see what any square was, or even where any square was? just thinking about it, these hours later is miserable. they really really need to change it to keep only the milder changes, and the random values it applies to your characters at the beginning of each battle. the way it distorted text, hiding information, and even the help guide was really interesting. but I had to quit and reload the game 3 times because it distorted the end of battle screen so much, i couldn't click the continue button. I wanted to try to describe the visual hell the joker commander created. It would randomly rotate squares and offset them around their starting point. when it was mild, this was fine and amusing. Where it got really bad was when they would uncap the offset distance, and every square on the board was pretty much in a random location. Where it got really really bad, was when the offsets would adjust mid match, and then the board would flip upside down and random tiles would be covered so I couldn't see them. god I can't stop my eyes from hurting thinking about it like 6 hours later. maybe if you enjoy acid or lsd or something it'd be an interesting expierience. I'm not even playing the game right now, and its like an acid flashback. as soon as im done editing this review, im going to uninstall the game and try to never think of those visuals again. right after I beat the run, I had to stop playing, turn off my screen and lay down for a 30 minutes I was so nauseated from looking at the screen. I'm thinking of doing it right now. even listening to the music now as I type this review is making me sick. and I have never gotten nauseous from playing a game before, and I've played 3k+ hours of vr games. and yes it is so bad that I've had to complain about it for the last 20 minutes I've been trying to type this review. So long as you don't play joker, this game is great. don't be like me. Don't play joker. enjoy the game! overall: enjoyable game go for the purchase if it looks interesting to you. (don't play the joker commander)

—————————————————————— 浅玩了一下，本作和作者前作genome guardian的局内外框架一致，但核心玩法从类吸血鬼幸存者的炮塔防御一转为战术战棋ROGUELIKE游戏。算得上是“旧瓶装新酒”了。 由于前作的局内外框架就很扎实，所以本作这方面依旧没什么问题，包括极强乐趣和策略性的局内构筑与足够丰富和动力的局外解锁内容。对于战棋玩法方面，本作引入了类似贪吃蛇的机制：大量棋子在移动时会拖出尾巴，不仅可以用于堵路，其体积也同时被视为血量。实际玩下来，不得不说这个机制既有创意，又有乐趣。不像其他战棋，血量总归多多益善。这游戏的血量越多，也会直观地表现为“臃肿”。并且这个设计也对走位多加了一层思考空间，不再仅是“别轻易进入敌人的攻击范围”。除此之外，大多机制到是各类战棋游戏中都能见到的元素。 只是...当把genome guardian的构筑思路，也放在这款战术战棋时，瞬间就...WOW.如果要类比的话，就当作玩家的单位初始只有4个职业（例如侦察、护卫、工兵、弓手）。但每个职业都可以至多转职3次，且每次转职有4个大方向（对应4个初始职业）。这样排列组合，足足提供总计60多个不同职业。并且构筑过程中，不仅要构筑所有单位的职业，还需要构筑单位的附加被动技能。此外，还可以构筑面向整支队伍的指挥官能力，以及对敌人进行构筑（特定波次结束后强制要求构筑敌人能力，相当于可由玩家自行选择如何强化敌人）。 这还只是局内的构筑，局外构筑还有着近30种指挥官（影响最大单位数量，单位职业、被动能力上限，以及独特的机制玩法）、局外天赋（从局外天赋库中选X个）、一次性道具（每场战斗可用一次的道具）、和一些开局的初始选项调整。另外，局外还有着适当的成长项和大量解锁项（常规的数值提升），以及多种不同的模式。 不得不说，前作就是自己最喜欢的类吸血鬼幸存者游戏之一，而本作有潜力成为自己最喜欢的战棋rougelike（想了想，也很少有战棋rogue，除了类TOME老派rogue和类陷阵之志这种重机制轻数值的游戏)。希望作者能和对待前作一样，持续维护更新。也希望这作能有更多销量。 —————————————— 打了快20小时，把游戏基本玩明白了。 这是一款“不平衡且构筑很容易被玩坏的游戏”，但游戏的乐趣就在于此，即“如何通过局内外构筑把游戏玩坏掉”。 游戏的终极目标，便是用所有指挥官打通最高难度。几乎每个指挥官的玩法思路都完全不同，且绝大多数指挥官的差异可以说是从底层改变游戏思路的程度。而恰当的局内外构筑则进一步强化指挥官的独特玩法，甚至使其长版能突破天际。 例如某个指挥官的能力是每轮都可以刷新gadget（道具）使用次数。正常来说，gadget（道具）一场战斗只能用一次，所以充其量是辅助工具。但对于这个指挥官，由于每轮都可以刷新使用次数，选择直接对敌人打1伤害的gadget（道具），构筑思路便是尽可能增加gadget（道具）的使用上限。而作为游戏核心的战斗单位，反而无足轻重。通过合适的构筑，甚至可以达成整局游戏战斗单位不移动不执行指令，纯靠gadget（道具）打伤把敌人全部收拾掉。 而像这样根本性改变游戏思路的指挥官，是绝大多数指挥官的设计思路。比如只能使用一个单位，但这个单位可以被构筑得很强的指挥官。比如单位自带辐射（自己掉血且对周围AOE），且辐射伤害增加但自身造成伤害削弱的指挥官。又比如能用很多单位，但单位的等级上限很低的指挥官。 且局外/局内的构筑也有大量有趣的设计，哪怕是纯粹加减数值，在这套体系下都能涌现出有趣的思路。比如这游戏会在3个固定时间点需要为敌人+buff，但这些buff通常也会有debuff效果。例如一个buff是攻击范围增加，但移动速度大幅降低。还有一个是血量[大小]上限增加，但移速降低。这俩配合在一起，可以让敌人的速度变为0，产生质变。随后通过超远程打伤害的单位或能力，就可以轻松把敌人一个个点掉。因此选的好的话，反而最终让敌人有着致命的短板与鸡肋的长板。配合自身构筑与指挥官特性，实现轻松碾压的效果。 总得来说，这绝对是款极其有趣且有特色的战棋roguelike游戏，强烈推荐！

Cell Command is a distinctive strategy roguelite developed and published by Alpherior that takes place on a microscopic battlefield where living cells wage war against dangerous viral threats. While many tactical games rely on familiar movement and combat systems, this title builds its identity around a highly original mechanic inspired by classic snake-style gameplay. Every movement causes a unit to grow longer, while attacks shorten its body. This simple rule fundamentally changes how players approach positioning, combat, and resource management, creating a strategic experience that feels fresh and inventive from the very beginning. The game's most compelling feature is its DNA-based customization system. Players combine different genetic components to create specialized cells with unique abilities and combat roles. Rather than locking players into a predefined roster, Cell Command encourages experimentation by allowing countless combinations and synergies. Some cellular units can construct pathways or bridges, others specialize in ranged attacks, while some focus on manipulating terrain or inflicting harmful status effects. This flexibility makes every run feel different and rewards creative thinking as players discover powerful interactions between various genetic traits. Combat revolves around more than simply defeating enemies. Since units physically change shape as they move and fight, the battlefield itself becomes a strategic puzzle. Long cell bodies can serve as shields, barriers, or tools for controlling enemy movement. Positioning takes on a new level of importance because every action permanently alters the layout of the encounter. Players are constantly making decisions about whether to extend a unit for greater control of the battlefield or shorten it through attacks to maintain flexibility. This dynamic creates a satisfying layer of tactical depth that separates the game from more conventional turn-based strategy titles. Progression is handled through a combination of roguelite systems and permanent upgrades. Successful runs unlock research opportunities, genetic enhancements, new commanders, and additional tools that expand future strategic options. The game also includes multiple difficulty levels and ascension-style challenges that increase complexity for experienced players. Enemy mutations ensure that strategies cannot be repeated endlessly without adjustment, forcing players to adapt and refine their approach. These systems provide strong long-term motivation and help maintain engagement over dozens of hours. Another major strength is the variety offered by the commander system. Different commanders introduce unique gameplay twists that significantly alter the flow of battle. Some emphasize mobility, others focus on aggressive tactics, and certain commanders feature unusual movement rules that require entirely new strategies. These differences make subsequent playthroughs feel meaningful rather than repetitive, giving players many reasons to revisit the game and explore alternative approaches. Visually, Cell Command embraces its biological setting with colorful environments and clear battlefield presentation. Despite dealing with microscopic organisms and genetic concepts, the game remains easy to read and understand during intense encounters. The artistic direction successfully balances scientific inspiration with a playful and accessible style. The audio package is equally impressive, featuring an extensive soundtrack that provides variety throughout long sessions and helps maintain the game's energetic atmosphere. The game also demonstrates a strong commitment to accessibility and convenience. Features such as controller support, cloud saving, Steam Deck compatibility, and colorblind-friendly options make the experience approachable for a wide audience. These additions may not directly affect gameplay, but they contribute to a polished package that feels thoughtfully designed from top to bottom. Cell Command is not necessarily aimed at players looking for quick or simple strategy gameplay. Its systems can initially seem unusual, and mastering the relationship between movement, shape manipulation, genetic customization, and battlefield control requires patience. However, players who enjoy discovering deep mechanics and experimenting with complex strategies will find a rewarding experience filled with meaningful decisions and creative possibilities. Ultimately, Cell Command succeeds because it takes a seemingly strange concept and transforms it into a compelling tactical adventure. The combination of roguelite progression, innovative battlefield mechanics, extensive customization, and strong replay value creates a game that stands out in an increasingly crowded genre. Alpherior has delivered a strategy title that feels genuinely original while still providing enough depth to keep dedicated players engaged for the long term. Cell Command is an imaginative and highly replayable strategy roguelite that combines unique mechanics with deep customization and rewarding tactical gameplay, making it a standout choice for fans seeking something different within the genre. Rating: 9/10
